headline: Strength is back — a long functional session broke the two-week gap. The restart run still stands alone, awaiting a second touch. Base intact, rhythm still forming.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The most meaningful change this week is that strength finally reappeared after being cold for over two weeks — and it landed as a substantial functional session, not a token check-in. That's one of the two long-standing gaps closing. Running, though, is still a single controlled restart touch; the second and third runs that would turn one contact into a weekly pattern haven't landed yet. The recent four-week running volume looks inflated by the Åre block's massive time-on-feet days, so the raw jump overstates current momentum — the picture right now is a big durability base sitting behind a very light restart. Steps stay high and consistent, keeping genuine daily background load steady even when structured running is thin. The load and recovery streams remain too sparse to read into. So the week is best described as re-establishing structure: strength restored, running still finding its feet.
sections.trends: The year-to-date distance is dramatically ahead of last year, which tells you the base built through 2026 is real and deep — the Åre block alone carried enormous vertical and time on feet. But the recent shape is irregular rather than building: a huge mountain block, then a week fully cold, then a single easy run. That burst-and-gap rhythm is the thing worth resolving, not the volume itself. For year-round hybrid readiness the base is in good shape; what's missing is the steady week-to-week spread that consolidates it rather than the peaks-and-troughs pattern that's dominated recently.
sections.threshold: The threshold read is now two months old and hasn't moved because nothing sustained has been run to refresh it. The Åre work was almost entirely low aerobic — deliberately so — and the restart run sat controlled and short. None of that challenges or updates the threshold picture. The stored fitness from a deep base is almost certainly intact, but until a sustained tempo effort appears you're working from an increasingly stale number. Treat the current figure as a floor, not a live reading.
sections.zones: The recent distribution makes sense for what each phase was doing: the Åre runs were almost pure Z1 time-on-feet, appropriate for ultra durability, and the two late-August runs showed genuine Z3/Z4 minutes — real intensity, not just an elevated average. The restart run sat honestly easy across Z1–Z2 with no grey-zone drift, exactly what a re-entry run should look like. The gap in the block isn't distribution quality — each session's intensity matched its intent — it's simply frequency. There's plenty of easy volume banked and a little sharpness recently; what's absent is any sustained threshold-band work.
sections.hr_comparison: The returning strength session came through without HR, so there's no shape to read on it directly, but the earlier functional sessions show the familiar pattern — mostly Z1 with intermittent pushes into Z2/Z3, consistent with circuit-style functional work rather than heavy low-rep lifting. Nothing in the source agreement between the running HR streams looks off; the easy runs and mountain days read coherently for their efforts.
sections.calendar: The calendar still shows the clustering pattern rather than spread — a dense block, a void, then isolated single sessions. The running streak persisting across many weeks tells you the underlying habit is durable even through the thin stretch, but the day-to-day placement remains lumpy. The encouraging signal this week is that strength landing on its own separate day begins to break that all-or-nothing clustering; whether running follows with mid-week touches is the thing that would actually flatten the pattern.
sections.personal_bests: The short-distance bests were all set in this same late-summer window last year, which is worth noting given the calendar — but current running is in restart mode with no sharpening yet, so none are within near reach right now. The base to chase them is present; the speed-specific work to convert it isn't happening this week.

watch_items: Watch whether strength converts from a single returning session into a repeating weekly presence, not another isolated touch.
Watch whether the restart run gains a second and third companion this week to establish an actual running rhythm.
Watch whether any sustained tempo finally appears to refresh the now two-month-stale threshold read.
Watch whether sessions start landing spread across days rather than clustering into bursts and gaps.
